key_insight: Ultrasonic nanocrystal surface modification significantly boosts the hardness and wear resistance of WC–Co–Cr thermal spray coatings, but the best spray route depends on the target failure mode.
engineering_relevance: Combining thermal spraying with UNSM is a practical surface-engineering strategy for extending the service life of steel components exposed to wear, impact, cavitation, and corrosion.
method: Deposited WC–Co–Cr coatings by detonation spraying, HVOF, and atmospheric plasma spraying.
Applied ultrasonic nanocrystal surface modification (UNSM) after coating deposition.
Evaluated microstructure and performance using SEM/EDS, hardness, tribology, abrasive/erosive/cavitation tests, corrosion/oxidation tests, and valve endurance testing.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports major performance gains after UNSM, including hardness up to 1596 HV and reduced wear metrics; APS+UNSM minimized several laboratory wear losses, while HVOF+UNSM performed best in valve endurance.
watch_item: Performance gains are mechanism-specific, so the preferred coating system may change with real service conditions and long-term durability requirements.
paper_title: Ultrasonic Surface Modification of WC-Co-Cr Thermal Spray Coatings: Microstructure, Mechanical Properties and Performance
